module.purpose: Provides a React hook that wraps TanStack DB's live queries with React Suspense support, enabling automatic data suspension and error boundary integration for reactive database queries.
module.summary: The useLiveSuspenseQuery hook bridges TanStack DB's reactive query system with React's Suspense mechanism. It accepts query functions, configuration objects, or pre-built collections, then throws promises during loading states that React's Suspense boundary catches. The hook ensures data is always defined (not optional), throws errors during initial load for Error boundaries, and returns stale data after successful loads if subsequent errors occur. It internally uses useLiveQuery for collection management and reactivity, maintaining referential equality and automatic re-subscription when dependencies change.
module.businessContext: Enables modern React data fetching patterns with automatic refetching and Suspense-based loading states. Critical for building responsive data-driven applications that need real-time updates without manual subscription management. Failure means broken loading states or unhandled promise rejections in Suspense-enabled UIs.

detail.signature: useLiveSuspenseQuery<TResult extends object, TKey extends string | number, TUtils extends Record<string, any>>(liveQueryCollection: Collection<TResult, TKey, TUtils> & SingleResult): { state: Map<TKey, TResult>; data: TResult | undefined; collection: Collection<TResult, TKey, TUtils> & SingleResult }
detail.returnType: { state: Map<TKey, TResult>; data: TResult | undefined; collection: Collection<TResult, TKey, TUtils> & SingleResult }
preconditions: The component using this hook is rendered within a React Suspense boundary.
The provided liveQueryCollection must not result in a disabled state (isEnabled must be true).
postconditions: Returns an object containing the query state (Map), current data (TResult | undefined), and the underlying collection.
The data property is undefined only until the collection's initial query resolves, at which point Suspense will suspend rendering.
invariants: The returned collection reference is stable across renders unless the input configuration/deps change.
edgeCases: If the liveQueryCollection becomes disabled (isEnabled: false), the hook throws a descriptive Error.
When the underlying collection reference changes (due to deps or config change), internal promise and ready state refs are reset.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Throws an Error if the provided query configuration results in a disabled state.

stateMutations: hasBeenReadyRef (mutable ref tracking if collection has been ready once)
detail.summary: A React hook that wraps useLiveQuery to provide Suspense integration for a live query collection. It throws an error if the query is disabled, enforcing the Suspense contract that data must always be defined.

specLiterals.value: useLiveSuspenseQuery does not support disabled queries (callback returned undefined/null). The Suspense pattern requires data to always be defined (T, not T | undefined). Solutions: 1) Use conditional rendering - don't render the component until the condition is met. 2) Use useLiveQuery instead, which supports disabled queries with the 'isEnabled' flag.
specLiterals.role: Error message thrown when the query is disabled, defining the exact contract violation and remediation options.

specTests.when: The hook is called within a component wrapped in React Suspense
specTests.then: The hook returns an object with state (Map), data (TResult), and collection. The Suspense boundary is not suspended.
The hook throws an Error with the specified message about disabled queries not being supported in Suspense.
